Define Problem Statement and perform Exploratory Data Analysis¶

  • Delhivery, India’s largest and fastest-growing fully integrated logistics provider, generates massive volumes of trip-level operational data through its data engineering pipelines. This raw data contains complex, multi-row trip records, segment-level routing information, distance and time metrics, and diverse categorical attributes related to transportation, routes, and logistics operations.

  • To support Delhivery’s mission of building an intelligent, high-quality, and efficient logistics operating system, the data must be converted into reliable, structured, and analysis-ready features. The challenge lies in cleaning, merging, interpreting, and engineering features from this fragmented dataset so that it can be used effectively for forecasting, optimization, and decision-making.

  • This project focuses on:

    • Cleaning and sanitizing raw trip data, handling missing values, inconsistencies, and outliers.
    • Merging multi-row trip entries into unified trip-level records using appropriate aggregations.
    • Engineering meaningful features from timestamps, location names, and routing information.
    • Evaluating relationships between actual vs. OSRM travel times and distances.
    • Standardizing, normalizing, and encoding columns for model readiness.
    • Deriving insights on network efficiency, route performance, and operational bottlenecks.

  • By transforming raw logistics data into high-quality analytical features, this work helps the Data Science team build robust forecasting models, optimize transportation routes, and drive better strategic and operational decisions—ultimately contributing to Delhivery’s competitive advantage in speed, efficiency, and profitability.

Introducing Feature 2 : od_time_diff_mins - Time taken between od_start_time and od_end_time¶

unique['od_start_time'] = pd.to_datetime(unique['od_start_time'])
unique['od_end_time'] = pd.to_datetime(unique['od_end_time'])

unique['od_time_diff_mins'] = (unique['od_end_time'] - unique['od_start_time']).dt.total_seconds() / (60)

Lowering the case of source_name and destination_name¶

In [ ]:
trip['destination_name'] = trip['destination_name'].str.lower()
trip['source_name'] = trip['source_name'].str.lower()

Defining Function to strip out State Name¶

In [ ]:
def place2state(x):
    state = x.split('(')[1] #splitting state based on"("
    return state[:-1] #removing ')' from end

Defining Function to strip out City¶

In [ ]:
def place2city(x):
    # removing state
    city = x.split(' (')[0]
    # picking the first city name
    city = city.split('_')[0]

    # Now dealing with edge cases
    # ['PNQ Pashan DPC', 'Bhopal MP Nagar', 'HBR Layout PC',
    # 'PNQ Rahatani DPC', 'Pune Balaji Nagar', 'Mumbai Antop Hill']

    if city == 'pnq vadgaon sheri dpc':
      return 'vadgaonsheri'
    elif city in ['pnq pashan dpc','pnq rahatani dpc', 'pune balaji nagar']:
      return 'pune'
    elif city == 'hbr layout pc' :
      return 'bengaluru'
    elif city == 'bhopal mp nagar' :
      return 'bhopal'
    elif city == 'mumbai antop hill' :
      return 'mumbai'
    else:
      return city

Defining Function to strip out Place¶

In [ ]:
def place2city_place(x):

    # We will remove state
    x = x.split(' (')[0]

    len1 = len(x.split('_'))

    if len1 >= 3:
        return x.split('_')[1]

    # Small cities have same city and place name
    if len1 == 2:
        return x.split('_')[0]

    return x.split(' ')[0]

Defining Function to strip out Place Code¶

In [ ]:
def place2code(x):
    # Removing State
    x = x.split(' (')[0]

    if len(x.split('_')) >= 3 :
        return x.split('_')[-1]

    return 'none'

Introducting 8 new features¶

In [ ]:
trip['source_state'] = trip['source_name'].apply(lambda x: place2state(x))
trip['source_city']  = trip['source_name'].apply(lambda x: place2city(x))
trip['source_place'] = trip['source_name'].apply(lambda x: place2city_place(x))
trip['source_code']  = trip['source_name'].apply(lambda x: place2code(x))

trip['destination_state'] = trip['destination_name'].apply(lambda x: place2state(x))
trip['destination_city']  = trip['destination_name'].apply(lambda x: place2city(x))
trip['destination_place'] = trip['destination_name'].apply(lambda x: place2city_place(x))
trip['destination_code']  = trip['destination_name'].apply(lambda x: place2code(x))

Handling the Outliers - Using IQR¶

In [ ]:
Q1 = trip[numeric_cols].quantile(0.25)
Q3 = trip[numeric_cols].quantile(0.75)
In [ ]:
IQR = Q3 - Q1
In [ ]:
trip = trip[~((trip[numeric_cols] < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR)) | (trip[numeric_cols] > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR))).any(axis=1)]

Hypothesis testing for start_scan_to_end_scan and od_time_diff_mins : to validate if both have the same mean or not¶

  • Ho : start_scan_to_end_scan and od_time_diff_mins have equal mean

  • Ha : start_scan_to_end_scan and od_time_diff_mins have different mean

  • Confidence Level : 95%

  • alpha : 0.05

In [ ]:
sstes = trip['start_scan_to_end_scan'].sample(5000)
otdm = trip['od_time_diff_mins'].sample(5000)
In [ ]:
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

test_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(sstes,otdm)
print('Test Statistic : ', test_stat)
print('P-Value : ', p_value)

Test Statistic :  1.8960159359814084
P-Value :  0.05798674287115718

  • As P-Value is greater than alpha, we fail to reject Ho

    • Ho : start_scan_to_end_scan and od_time_diff_mins have the equal mean

  • We can conclude that there is no significant difference between start_scan_to_end_scan and od_time_diff_mins

Business Insights¶

  • Max orders are coming from state Maharashtra and the top 3 contributor cities are Mumbai, Bhiwandi, Pune
  • Least orders were booked in Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Himachal Pradesh
  • At city level max orders are coming from Bengaluru, Gurgaon, Mumbai
  • At city level min orders were placed Jetpur, Kadiri, Vadakkencherry
  • Some cities appear under multiple names. Eg: Mumbai has been referred to as Mumbai, Mumbai hub, Lower Parel etc. If these different city names identify the same city, it could alter which city ranks highest in deliveries.
  • Most of the orders are within the state (86.67%)
  • Busiest route is IND562132AAA (bangalore_nelmngla_h (karnataka)) to IND560300AAA (bengaluru_kgairprt_hb (karnataka))
    • Average distance : 28.022 Km
    • Average time taken : 87.87 mins
  • Max orders were booked on Wednesday followed by Saturday
  • There is a significant difference between OSRM and actual parameters

Recommendation¶

There is a need to:¶

  • Revisit information fed to routing engine for trip planning.Check for discrepancies with transporters, if the routing engine is configured for optimum results.

  • North, South and West Zones corridors have significant traffic of orders. But, we have a smaller presence in Central, Eastern and North-Eastern zone. However it would be difficult to conclude this, by looking at just 2 months data. It is worth investigating and increasing our presence in these regions.

  • More campaign / advertisement in the states with less orders like Arunachal, Nagaland, Himachal etc.

  • From state point of view, we have heavy traffic in Mahrashtra followed by Karnataka. This is a good indicator that we need to plan for resources on ground in these 2 states on priority. Especially, during festive seasons.

  • Some cities appear under multiple names. Eg: Mumbai has been referred to as Mumbai, Mumbai hub, Lower Parel etc. If these different city names identify the same city, it could alter which city ranks highest in deliveries. Hence, it is recommended to clarify whether these names should be consolidated under one city or treated as separate locations
